text:
juno: heads up — ap-southeast1 is showing a cluster-wide NVMe latency hump coinciding with nightly ephemeral-scrub jobs starting at 23:00 local. GPU attach errors creeping to ~4%.

ezra: any correlation with network or cpu?

juno: checked — CPU and net look fine. iostat snapshot from affected node:
```
Device:        rrqm/s wrqm/s   r/s   w/s  rMB/s  wMB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm  %util
nvme0n1         0.00   6.00  22.0  310.0   3.2    9.4    37.0    18.9  55.1   25.4  62.1  2.80  88.7
```

ops-bot: ALERT: ephemeral-scrub:region_ap-southeast1 iops_spike (2026-03-20T23:02Z) — 11.6k ops, p99 latency 120ms :warning:

kevin: that's high. Are the janitors doing full fsync per-file? We saw write amplification last month when fsyncs were unbatched.

sophie: correct — the current janitor implementation does per-file sync on delete windows. We can flip to batched commits with `--sync-window=5s` to reduce syscalls. Risk: longer window until deletion durable.

ejra: typo — ezra*

ezra: agreed on batch commit, but we need immediate stopgap. Can we throttle scrub IO with cgroup blkio throttle or set ionice?

kevin: ionice/renice helps userland scheduling but doesn't protect against device queue saturation from many small writes. blkio.throttle.max_bytes_for_device would help. I can push a DaemonSet that sets a blkio throttle for pods with label `app=janitor` to 50MB/s for scrub period.

juno: Do it, but test on canary nodes first. Also reduce janitor parallelism via config: `toolctl config set scrub.parallel_workers 3` — lower from default 10.

sophie: making a quick feature flag: scrub.batch_sync=true and scrub.sync_window_ms=5000. I'll toggle on canary after throttle applied.

ops-bot: ACTION: creating incident INC-2026-1123 and paging oncall SRE.

kevin: patch DS ready. Command to apply to canary: `kubectl -n infra apply -f scrub-blkio-canary.yaml` (sets blkio throttle to 50MB/s for device 259:0). Rolling now.

ezra: monitoring p99 attach latencies and kubelet evict logs.

ops-bot: EVENT: blkio throttle applied to 3 canary nodes at 2026-03-20T23:08Z

juno: canary results: nvme util dropped from ~89% -> 42% and attach failures back to ~0.6% within 60s. Nice work.

sophie: flipped batch commits on canary. Observed write syscall rate drop ~4x.

kevin: rolling throttle to rest of ap-southeast1 with a staged 10-node ramp every 30s to avoid API storms.

ezra: cost note — lower concurrency + throttles extend scrub duration. Expected extra background IO window ~+1.1% cost for region. That's acceptable for now.

juno: long-term items: 1) implement scrub.batch_sync with bounded memory to avoid OOM, 2) add per-region blkio knobs in platform config, 3) rework janitor to scan incrementally with persistent cursor to avoid rewalking. I'll file INFRA-4291/INFRA-4292.

ops-bot: MONITOR: ap-southeast1 nvme_util 44% p99_attach_latency 72ms at 2026-03-20T23:20Z

sophie: note — test customers in the region (alpha-dedicated) reported transient 5-8s warmups during ramp. CS notified.

ejra: (again ezra) small nit: scrub.blkio_device currently expects major:minor; we should accept device UUID to be less fragile across kernel changes. Adding to INFRA-4292.

ezra: thanks — monitoring for 45m. If green we revert parallel_workers to 10 and keep batch_sync enabled.

kevin: leaving follow-up: plan to upstream a safe blkio controller helper in our infra library so we can reuse for other heavy background jobs.

juno: ok wrapping up — I'll paste short postmortem and link graphs in INC-2026-1123. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
